text: I told my therapist I have commitment issues. She said, see you never.
My therapist says I have a preoccupation with revenge. We'll see about that.
I bought a thesaurus yesterday. It is already bored of my synonyms.
The universe is expanding. So is my inbox. Only one of those is optional.
I am on a seafood diet. I see food and I eat it.
I asked the librarian for a book on paranoia. She whispered that they are right behind you.
Every time I try to save money, it finds me.
I named my dog Five Miles so I can honestly say I walk Five Miles every day.
The best thing about time travel is that I already told that joke.
I put my phone in airplane mode. It still refused to fly.
My sleep app says I snored for forty-one minutes. Rude. I was awake for most of it.
Nothing says I have my life together quite like cereal for dinner on a Tuesday.
I do not need a hairstylist. My pillow gives me a new look every single morning.
My houseplants are alive purely out of spite.
I have a photographic memory but no film.
The speed of light is fast. The speed of my Monday is faster.
My fitness tracker says I did eight thousand steps. Six of them were trips to the fridge.
I asked the GPS to take me somewhere I have never been. It said that describes every trip.
They call it rush hour, and yet nobody is moving.
I finally learned to live within my means. Unfortunately my means are eleven rupees.
My dog understands every word I say. He simply disagrees.
It is not procrastination if you enjoy the panic.
I am not arguing. I am explaining why I am right, loudly, with gestures.
Coffee first. Sentences later.
I tried to catch some fog. I mist.
The shovel was a ground-breaking invention.
I used to be indecisive. Now I am not so sure.
Some people graduate with honours. I graduated with an attendance record.
My bank account is like a sieve. It holds nothing but holes and regret.
I am reading a book on anti-gravity. It is impossible to put down.
Parallel lines have so much in common. Shame they will never meet.
I asked IT for a password nobody could guess. They gave me my own birthday.
Winter is coming. So is my heating bill. Only one of them is unwelcome.
I do not always lose my keys, but when I do, I am already late.
Ice cubes are just water that went to finishing school.
My phone battery and I have the same approach to plans. Ten percent and falling.
Cloud storage is just someone else's computer, worrying about my files.
Every group project has one person who does everything and one who says let us circle back. I am at peace with which one I am.
I told my computer I needed a break. Now it will not stop showing me beach photos.
My calendar has a meeting with myself. I have already rescheduled it twice.
I do not need an alarm clock. My ambitions wake me at six. So does my neighbour's drill, at seven.
The wifi password is the true test of a friendship.
I have not lost weight. I have simply redistributed it into my face.
Autocorrect has rewritten my texts so often that I now consider it a co-author.
My laptop fan spins up whenever I open too many tabs, which is to say always.
I bought a mug that says world's okayest developer. It was the best I could do.
There are two kinds of people: those who back up their data, and those who will.
I told the weather app it was wrong. It has not spoken to me since.
My phone has a dark mode. So do I.
Every notification is just a stranger asking for a piece of your afternoon.
I do not have a short attention span. I have a long attention span that I choose not to use.
The meeting could have been an email. The email could have been nothing.
My favourite exercise is a cross between a lunge and a crunch. I call it lunch.
I keep my phone on silent because my thoughts are loud enough.
Nothing humbles a person faster than a spreadsheet someone else built.
I have reached the age where my back goes out more than I do.
Somewhere, a developer is one semicolon away from a very long night.
I asked for a sign. The universe sent a loading spinner.
Optimism is just pessimism that has not been tested yet.
I do not snore. I dream that I am a motorcycle.
The snooze button is the only commitment I have ever honoured.
My handwriting has a doctorate in being illegible.
I clean my desk when I am avoiding work. It is now spotless and I have done nothing.
Every shirt I own is either laundry or a costume.
The journey of a thousand miles begins with a slightly uncomfortable chair.
You miss one hundred percent of the naps you do not take.
Do not count the days. Make the days count. Then take a nap and recount.
Rise and grind. Or rise and do not. The sun will do its job either way.
Success is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent forgetting you left the stove on.
Bloom where you are planted, unless you planted yourself in concrete.
Every expert was once a beginner who refused to read the instructions.
Leap and the net will appear. If it does not, you now have excellent core strength.
Your only limit is you. Also gravity. Mostly gravity.
Do one thing every day that scares you. Mine is opening the electricity bill.
Hustle until your haters ask if you are okay.
The best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago. The second best time is after chai.
Champions keep playing until they get it right. Legends keep playing until they get it wrong twice.
Wake up. Be awesome. Go back to sleep. Repeat as needed.
Dream big, but please, for the love of sleep, not at three in the morning.
You are capable of amazing things, mostly between eleven and four.
Nothing worth having comes easy. Except dust. Dust comes very easy.
Be the change you wish to see, but first check whether the change is refundable.
Greatness is not a destination. It is a wrong turn you refuse to correct.
You get out what you put in. I put in chai. I got out chai.
The early bird gets the worm, but the second mouse gets the cheese.
Believe in yourself, mostly because nobody else can do it for you at this hour.
Every day is a gift. Some days it is a gift you would like to return.
Failure is simply the opportunity to begin again, this time with more snacks.
You are one choice away from a completely different life. Choose the paneer.
Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most. Now is also valid.
If it does not challenge you, it will not change you. If it challenges you too much, cancel it.
Slow progress is still progress. So is standing still with a cup of coffee.
The mountain is not tall. It is simply very committed to being tall.
Do what you love and you will never work a day in your life, said nobody with a deadline.
Energy flows where attention goes, which explains a great deal about my inbox.
You cannot pour from an empty cup. Fill it. Then find a second cup for backup.
Great minds discuss ideas. Average minds discuss events. Small minds discuss the office thermostat.
Somewhere there is a version of you that went to bed at ten. Respect them.
The universe is not testing you. It is simply not paying attention.
Trust the timing of your life, but also set an alarm.
You do not find yourself. You build yourself, badly, over many years.
Everything happens for a reason. Sometimes the reason is that you did not read the instructions.
Stay hungry, stay foolish, stay hydrated.
A comfort zone is a beautiful place, but nothing ever grows there except mildew.
When one door closes, another opens. Usually it is the fridge.
